title: Trace-fusion loadbook and ramp policy
body:
Purpose:
This note defines a repeatable harness and methodology we call "trace-fusion" for throughput benchmarking of the serving runtime. Trace-fusion mixes short-duration real-user trace slices with synthetic steady tails so that we can exercise both realistic variability and large sustained occupancy. The goal is reproducible throughput claims and clear attribution of bottlenecks (network, kernel, batching, KV-cache).

Scope and motivation:
- Target: 1–100k qps experiments across model sizes and quantization paths.
- Problem we address: purely synthetic Poisson or constant-rate load misses correlation structure in real traffic; pure trace replay doesn’t scale to stress steady-state throughput or isolate long-tail thermal effects.
- Trace-fusion fuses a set of short authentic trace snippets (10–60s) sampled from production traces, and stitches them into a controlled ramp/steady window filled with synthetic token-length distributions matching each trace snippet.

High level recipe:
1) Curate trace shards: pick N short trace shards (10–60s) from daily production sample, label with median seq_len, client mix, and percentile qps. Keep a holdout shard set (20%) for later regression checks.
2) Synthesize tails: build a synthetic steady stream generator whose sequence length histogram is the shard-weighted distribution.
3) Ramp policy: apply a staggered ramp (see below) to reach target occupancy while injecting shards at known offsets (anchor points).
4) Repeatable RNG: use an entropy-controlled RNG seed per run and per shard. Save seeds with run metadata.
5) Observability capture: collect per-request latency, GPU utilization, kernel-level stalls (counters), allocator stats, KV cache hit/miss, batching counts, and loadgen client-side timing.

Load matrix and configs (example):
- axes: target qps, shard-mix (heavy/median/light), tail skew (long/short), model variant (fp16/4bit), batch policy (auto/manual), priming enabled (yes/no).
- canonical runs: 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% of rated capacity for each GPU type.
- run length: 20 minute warmup + 60 minute steady collection. Capture at 1s granularity.

Staggered ramp policy (why):
- Single-step ramps destabilize batching and thermal steady state. We use a 4-stage stagger with dwell windows to allow kernel selection & batch coalescing to equilibrate.
- Example timings (target 10k qps):
  * T0: 0->1k qps, 3m dwell
  * T1: 1k->4k qps, 5m dwell
  * T2: 4k->8k qps, 7m dwell
  * T3: 8k->10k qps, 5m dwell then enter steady 60m collection

Shard injection anchors and holdout usage:
- During dwell windows we inject one held-out production shard at a deterministic offset to measure how real variability affects batching and latency tails.
- Holdout shards are only replayed verbatim in 1 of 3 repeat runs to detect regression.

Warmup and repeatability checklist (must follow for each experiment):
- Clear KV-cache (or record initial hit-rate) and document cache policy used.
- Ensure model weights are resident and query a short priming prompt set (3x) to populate attention caches. Record priming latency.
- Set RNG seeds for both client load generators and any in-runtime randomized schedulers. Store seed bundle with run metadata.
- Preheat GPU thermal profile: run a CPU/GPU noop kernel for 2 minutes if previous run was idle >30m.
- Sync clocks across clients and collectors (NTP or chrony); assert max clock skew <50ms.

Data to record per run (minimum):
- run_id, seed_bundle, git_sha_loadgen, git_sha_runtime, model_variant, instance_type, kernel_choice, quantization_profile, start/end timestamps, ramp timeline, injected_shards metadata (ids), priming_set ids.
- time-series (1s): qps, p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/s, batch_size distribution, batching wait time, GPU_util, GPU_mem, power, eviction_count, kv_hit_rate.

Analysis heuristics and fault fingerprints:
- Batching starvation: if batch_size distribution variance high and mean < expected, correlate with client inter-arrival CV and kernel batch-delay metric.
- Kernel thrashing: if latency step changes correlate with kernel_choice flips in logs, mark as kernel-selection instability; rerun with fixed kernel policy.
- KV-cache-induced tail: p99 increases when kv_hit_rate drops; plot p99 vs kv_hit_rate in 30s windows.
- Thermal throttling: GPU_util drops while power limit events increase; confirm with host powercap logs.

Loadgen configuration example (plain text snippet):
loadgen:
  threads: 128
  clients_per_thread: 4
  seed: 123456789
  interarrival: "mixture" # configured per-shard
  shards_file: /traces/shard_manifest.json
  tail_generator:
    type: histogram_resample
    target_histogram: /tmp/trace_fusion_hist.json
  jitter_injection_ms: 3
  clock_sync: true
  metrics_endpoint: prometheus://loadgen-metrics:9090

Success criteria and stability gates:
- Repeatability: two independent runs with same seed and config must have <5% difference in mean throughput and <10% difference in p99.
- Thermal stable: GPU freq and power metrics converge within first 10 minutes of steady window.
- Regression detection: holdout-shard p99 must not degrade more than 15% compared to baseline anchor run.

Common failure modes encountered in prior experiments:
- Client-side pacing jitter: misconfigured event loop in loadgen introduces microbursts; fixed by increasing threads and using sleep-until instead of sleep-for.
- Mis-specified seq_len histograms: synthetic tail mismatch causing unexpected batching behavior; mitigate by per-shard histogram calibration pass.
- Hidden network queues: observed when host NIC buffers cause inflated tail latencies; use pcap and host tcp_metrics to diagnose.

Practical notes and tips:
- Save full run tarball (loadgen logs, runtime logs, metrics, GPU counters) with retention policy for at least 90 days for forensic comparisons.
- When trying quantized kernels, constrain runs to shorter steady windows until kernel selection is validated.
- Use pinned CPU and IRQ affinities for loadgen clients to reduce client-side variance.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we include a mid-run kernel-lock experiment (force a kernel choice for first 5 minutes only) to isolate kernel-selection costs?
- Automate shard selection by anomaly score so anchors reflect recent traffic shifts.
- Add a thermal soak variant (4 hour run) to capture long-term drift for enterprise SLAs.

Next steps:
- Implement trace-fusion mode in loadgen repo (PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/loadgen/pull/78).
- Run canonical matrix on p4d and a100 fleets next quarter and publish internal throughput claims with attached run tarballs.

References and pointers:
- CONFLUENCE-5642: trace sampling guide
- JIRA-INF-1234: loadgen trace-fusion epic
- github.com/redwood-inference/loadgen/tree/trace-fusion (draft impl)

Author notes: this is intentionally prescriptive to make bench runs less ad-hoc. Expect iterative tuning after first 30 runs.
